CARD CAPTIONS — PRIMARY (migrated 2026-08-30): Ontario's Lake Country: Four nights, and the two bases are 90 minutes apart. | Old Quebec & Montreal: Four nights, three hours apart on the 20. | The Cabot Trail: A 298 km loop; three nights based at Ingonish.

CARD CAPTIONS — NATURE (migrated 2026-08-30): Muskoka Lakes: Cottage country empties out after Labour Day. | Algonquin Provincial Park: Colour peaks late September to mid-October. | Bay of Fundy / Hopewell Rocks: Only walkable at low tide — times posted at the gate daily. | Cape Breton Highlands National Park: The Skyline boardwalk is 8 km return, mostly flat. | Prince Edward Island North Shore: Confederation Bridge tolls on the way out, not in.

CARD CAPTIONS — CITIES (migrated 2026-08-30): Toronto: Two nights at the start; the island ferry has the best view of it. | Ottawa: Parliament Hill and the ByWard Market are a ten-minute walk apart. | Montreal: Mount Royal is a 30-minute climb from downtown, and free. | Quebec City: The old town is walkable end to end; park once. | Halifax: Peggy's Cove is 45 minutes away — go early or late for the light. | Lunenburg: Easy half-day from Halifax, often combined with Peggy's Cove.

CARD CAPTIONS — FOOD (migrated 2026-08-30): Poutine: La Banquise in Montreal does thirty versions, around the clock. | Montreal Smoked Meat: The famous delis are cash-only and queue out the door. | Beaver Tails: The ByWard Market stand in Ottawa is where the chain started. | Maple Syrup & Fudge: Graded by colour — darker means later in the season and stronger. | Halifax Donair: King of Donair on Quinpool Road claims the original, from 1973. | Fast Food & Big-City Eating: Both Chinatowns are walkable from the centre of town.

CARD CAPTIONS — THINGS TO DO (migrated 2026-08-30): Montmorency Falls: Fifteen minutes from Quebec City; there is a zipline across the gorge too. | Île d'Orléans Food Road: 67 km round the island — half a day with stops. | A Maple Sugar Shack: Autumn shacks are quieter than the spring rush; most are around Quebec City. | The Toronto Islands Ferry: Ferries from Jack Layton Terminal; last boat back is late. | Driving the Confederation Bridge: Free going over; the toll is collected when you leave the island. | Whale Boats off Cape Breton: Pleasant Bay is the main departure point — ring the day before.

SEASONALITY (verified 2026-08-30, web search): 'A Maple Sugar Shack' was cut and replaced with 'The Muskoka Cranberry Harvest'. The taffy-on-snow ritual it described needs an actual sugaring season (sap running, snow on the ground) — that's late winter/early spring, not October, so it never fit this trip's window. Johnston's Cranberry Marsh & Muskoka Lakes Farm & Winery (Bala, Muskoka) runs its cranberry harvest from about two weekends before Canadian Thanksgiving through the end of October, which covers the trip's Muskoka leg (days 4-5) on a late-September start, and also makes apple-cranberry cider on site. No Wikimedia photo of the actual Bala marsh was found, so the card image is a generic wet-harvest photo (Massachusetts) — caption describes only what it shows, not the specific farm.
title: Ontario, Quebec & the Maritimes: A Canadian East Coast Road Trip
brief: Three weeks of easy driving through Canada's prettiest fall colours — vibrant city life in Toronto, lazy lake days in Muskoka, charming old towns in Quebec, and the wild, windswept coastlines of the Maritimes. Red and gold forests, lighthouses, red-sand beaches, and comfort food the whole way.

facts.bestSeason: Late September–early October, for peak fall colours
facts.timezone: Eastern Time, with Atlantic Time (+1h) in Nova Scotia/PEI/New Brunswick
facts.driving: Right-hand traffic, excellent highways, long but easy distances

primary.heading: City, cottage, and the coast
primary.intro: Three distinct stretches: a big-city and lake-country start in Ontario, French Canada through the middle, then the Atlantic provinces where the road runs along the cliffs for hours at a time.

nature.heading: Maple forest, lake and tideline
nature.intro: This is the fall-colour trip. Sugar maple turns red here rather than gold, and the colour runs all the way from Algonquin east to Cape Breton.

cities.heading: Two languages, five different downtowns
cities.intro: Toronto's glass and Montreal's brick, Quebec City's walled old town, and harbour towns out east where everything faces the water.

food.heading: Gravy, smoked meat and maple
food.intro: Comfort food is the whole idiom — fries buried under cheese curds, sandwiches piled past reason, and sugar in forms you haven't met before.

why.heading: What the east coast gives you
why.intro: Peak colour, effortless driving, no language barrier worth the name, and a coastline most people never get round to.

thingsToDo.heading: Waterfalls, ferries and sugar
thingsToDo.intro: Nearly all of this is turn-up-and-do: a ferry, a bridge, a farm road, a cable car over a waterfall. Only the whale boats want a phone call the day before.

itinerary.description: Land in the evening, sleep near the airport, and start the trip well rested.
The Distillery District, the waterfront, and Kensington Market's colourful mess of shops.
Slow down at a lakeside cottage — swims, quiet sunsets, and Algonquin's maples an hour away.
Parliament Hill, riverside parkland, the canal, and the ByWard Market for browsing.
Cobblestones and murals, a walk up Mount Royal, and the best smoked meat and bagels anywhere.
A walled old town straight out of Europe, a waterfall taller than Niagara, and a food island next door.
The road-trip night: a long, pretty drive east and a motel on the Saint John river.
Red cliffs and rolling farmland, reached across a 13 km bridge, with Hopewell Rocks on the way.
One of the world's great coastal drives, with easy cliff hikes and fishing villages below.
A friendly harbour city, the postcard lighthouse at Peggy's Cove, and Lunenburg down the coast.

primaryHighlights.title: Ontario's Lake Country
primaryHighlights.description: Big-city energy in Toronto, or quiet lakeside days at a cottage — an easy, relaxed start to the trip.
primaryHighlights.caption: Sailboat on a Muskoka lake

primaryHighlights.title: Old Quebec & Montreal
primaryHighlights.description: Montreal's energy and Quebec City's fairy-tale Old Town — a taste of Europe far from home.
primaryHighlights.caption: Château Frontenac at dusk

primaryHighlights.title: The Cabot Trail
primaryHighlights.description: Red dunes, cliffside roads, lighthouses, and fishing villages — the scenery you'll be showing off in photos for years.
primaryHighlights.caption: Peggy's Cove harbour and lighthouse

natureHighlights.title: Muskoka Lakes
natureHighlights.description: Ontario's beloved lake district — swim, relax, and enjoy the water at your own pace.
natureHighlights.caption: Autumn dock on a Muskoka lake

natureHighlights.title: Algonquin Provincial Park
natureHighlights.description: Easy forest trails and lookout points over lakes surrounded by maple and pine.
natureHighlights.caption: Lake view from Algonquin's lookout rocks

natureHighlights.title: Bay of Fundy / Hopewell Rocks
natureHighlights.description: Towering flowerpot rock formations standing on a sea bed that empties and refills twice a day.
natureHighlights.caption: Hopewell Rocks flowerpot formations

natureHighlights.title: Cape Breton Highlands National Park
natureHighlights.description: A boardwalk trail along green cliffs, ending at one of the best ocean viewpoints in Canada.
natureHighlights.caption: Cabot Trail's coastal switchbacks

natureHighlights.title: Prince Edward Island North Shore
natureHighlights.description: Red cliffs, soft sand beaches, and farmland green as far as you can see.
natureHighlights.caption: Red cliffs on PEI's north shore

cityHighlights.title: Toronto
cityHighlights.description: A big, easy-to-love city with waterfront walks and great shopping.
cityHighlights.caption: Toronto skyline from the harbour

cityHighlights.title: Ottawa
cityHighlights.description: Grand government architecture, riverside parkland, and a lively market for browsing.
cityHighlights.caption: Parliament Hill's Peace Tower

cityHighlights.title: Montreal
cityHighlights.description: Old Montreal's grand basilica and cobblestone streets, right by the murals and cafés of the Plateau.
cityHighlights.caption: Notre-Dame Basilica at night

cityHighlights.title: Quebec City
cityHighlights.description: The storybook, castle-like Château Frontenac towering over the Old Town — like stepping into Europe without leaving Canada.
cityHighlights.caption: Château Frontenac in winter

cityHighlights.title: Halifax
cityHighlights.description: A hilltop star-shaped fort overlooking a friendly harbour city — a relaxed spot to end the trip.
cityHighlights.caption: The star-shaped Halifax Citadel

cityHighlights.title: Lunenburg
cityHighlights.description: A UNESCO fishing town of bright wooden houses stacked up a hillside, an hour down the coast from Halifax.
cityHighlights.caption: Waterfront warehouses in Lunenburg

culinaryHighlights.title: Poutine
culinaryHighlights.description: Fries, cheese curds and gravy — Canada's ultimate comfort food, and impossible to have just once.
culinaryHighlights.caption: A plate of poutine

culinaryHighlights.title: Montreal Smoked Meat
culinaryHighlights.description: Piled-high sandwiches at legendary, no-frills delis.
culinaryHighlights.caption: A hand-piled smoked meat sandwich

culinaryHighlights.title: Beaver Tails
culinaryHighlights.description: Fried-dough hand-stretched pastries served hot with sweet toppings like cinnamon sugar or chocolate.
culinaryHighlights.caption: A BeaverTails pastry in Ottawa

culinaryHighlights.title: Maple Syrup & Fudge
culinaryHighlights.description: Fresh maple syrup and maple taffy on snow, straight from the source.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Maple fudge in a display case

culinaryHighlights.title: Halifax Donair
culinaryHighlights.description: A beloved local sandwich, sweet and spiced — the perfect last bite before flying home.
culinaryHighlights.caption: A donair wrap with creamy sauce

culinaryHighlights.title: Fast Food & Big-City Eating
culinaryHighlights.description: Five Guys and A&W on every highway exit, and in Toronto and Montreal some of the best ramen, dumplings and Korean food outside Asia.
culinaryHighlights.caption: Chinatown street on Spadina Avenue

thingsToDo.title: Montmorency Falls
thingsToDo.description: A waterfall taller than Niagara with a suspension bridge straight across the top, a cable car up the side, and a staircase down the cliff.
thingsToDo.caption: Suspension bridge over Montmorency Falls

thingsToDo.title: Île d'Orléans Food Road
thingsToDo.description: A single loop road around a farm island in the St Lawrence, lined with cider houses, chocolate makers, bakeries and cheese sheds.
thingsToDo.caption: Lavender rows on Île d'Orléans

thingsToDo.title: The Muskoka Cranberry Harvest
thingsToDo.description: A bog floods bright red as the cranberries are shaken loose and gathered for harvest right through October, followed by a taste of the apple and cranberry ciders made on the farm.
thingsToDo.caption: A flooded cranberry bog at harvest

thingsToDo.title: The Toronto Islands Ferry
thingsToDo.description: A fifteen-minute crossing to a car-free island with the best view of the skyline, plus rental bikes and a boardwalk.
thingsToDo.caption: Downtown Toronto from the ferry

thingsToDo.title: Driving the Confederation Bridge
thingsToDo.description: Thirteen kilometres of bridge over open sea to Prince Edward Island — about twelve minutes with water on both sides the whole way.
thingsToDo.caption: Driving across Confederation Bridge

thingsToDo.title: Whale Boats off Cape Breton
thingsToDo.description: Humpbacks, minke and pilot whales feed off the northern tip of the island, and the boats run right through October.
thingsToDo.caption: A whale-watching boat at sea

otherPerks: Peak maple colour — reds and oranges rather than the gold you get in the Alps, lasting for weeks
New type of scenery (atlantic coastal) in a familiar setting
A similar fast food and shopping experience to the US
Crowds thin out after Labour Day while everything stays open
Diner breakfasts, delis and roadside chip trucks between every city
Long distances, but empty roads and some of the best surfaces anywhere
Two languages and no friction — English works everywhere, including Quebec
A proper road-trip night in New Brunswick, motel and all
